AbstractText.Label: OBJECTIVE
AbstractText.content: Consequences of OSAS include excessive daytime sleepiness, divided sleep architecture, impaired neurocognitive performance, and significant psychosocial disruption. In this study we aimed to evaluate sleep spindles changes before and after PAP treatment in patient with OSA.

AbstractText.Label: METHODS
AbstractText.content: Seventy-three consecutive patients (M/F:61/12) who applied to Sleep Disorders Center of Inonu University Hospital and met the inclusion criteria were enrolled to this study. Full-night polysomnography and CPAP titration were performed.

AbstractText.Label: RESULTS
AbstractText.content: Mean AHI were detected as 43,8±24,4 and mean oxygen saturation was 79% in patients under full-night PSG. Singificant increasing were observed on spindle count under CPAP titration (192±98.vs 347±165 per hour p<0.001)) and also significant increasing was recorded on oxygen saturation (79±15 vs 94±4% p<0.001).

AbstractText.Label: CONCLUSION
AbstractText.content: Both spindle count and oxygen saturation were recorded to be significantly increased under CPAP titration while there was a significant decrease in apnea-hypopnea. We have shown that significant increase in number of spindles can be achieved with CPAP treatment, those to be decreased in patient with OSA. Number of spindles may play a role as an indicator of better outcome in OSA patients.
